evidence_map.basis_quote: A September 2016 New York Times investigation, republished by the Las Vegas Sun, examined public subsidies for Donald Trump’s New York real-estate projects. It reported that Trump sought a 10-year property-tax abatement under New York City’s 421-a program for Trump Tower, a luxury residential and commercial building. The city initially rejected the application, but the New York Court of Appeals later ruled that the city had improperly erected a barrier to the program’s benefit. The city Finance Department valued the 421-a benefit for Trump Tower at $22.5 million. The article separately reports a later $15 million tax break under another program for renovations to the tower’s commercial space; that amount is not part of the 421-a figure. The program was created to stimulate housing construction, but the supplied reporting does not identify an affordable-unit commitment attached to this particular abatement or establish that Trump violated the program. The revised title and description focus on the documented tax benefit and court history, avoiding an unsupported claim about affordable-housing obligations or misuse.
